gating: Sensitive ⚑ (high-stakes safeguarding; never outs anyone; careful triage)
note: Identity, orientation & respect (UNESCO 3.1, 1.3, 7.1). New v2 build, Chapter 5. People differ in who they are and who they love, and every person deserves dignity, respect and safety, that part isn't a debate. Built on one non-negotiable: respect is a value, not a debate. Teaches understanding and busts harmful myths WITHOUT disparaging anyone's family or beliefs; separates honest belief-differences (respected) from the dignity floor (upheld). Supports anyone questioning, with no pressure to label and complete confidentiality; never outs or infers anyone. Non-explicit. Builds on g7/g25; links g27/g31. India: consensual same-sex relations decriminalised (2018), NALSA recognised transgender persons, dignity & equality are constitutional values, and India has its own long-acknowledged diversity traditions; framed around settled values, not contested policy. Routes distress/family-conflict to a trusted adult/counsellor, Tele-MANAS 14416, KIRAN 1800-599-0019, Childline 1098. Sharing anything is always the person's own choice.

categories.dignity-for-all: Dignity for all: respect in action

evidenceBase: People vary naturally in their sexual orientation (who they are attracted to) and their gender identity (their own internal sense of their gender); this diversity is a natural, longstanding part of humanity across cultures and history, including India's own long-acknowledged traditions. Neither sexual orientation nor gender identity is a mental illness, a choice, a phase, contagious or a foreign import, the scientific consensus (WHO ICD-11 and the APA removed them from illness classifications) is settled (WHO; UNESCO KC3.1)

Respect is a value, not a debate: everyone deserves dignity, respect and safety regardless of orientation or identity. In India this rests on settled constitutional values, consensual same-sex relations between adults were decriminalised in 2018 (Navtej Johar), the NALSA judgment recognised transgender persons, and dignity, equality and privacy are guaranteed rights. The game frames everything around those settled values, not contested policy, so it neither campaigns nor disparages anyone's beliefs; you do not have to agree with everyone to treat everyone with dignity and keep them safe

Safety is paramount for potentially vulnerable youth: the game never outs, records or infers anyone's orientation or identity and never urges disclosure, whether, when and to whom anyone shares anything is entirely their own choice, best made with trusted support. Anyone questioning is told it is okay to be unsure, there is no pressure to label, they are not broken and not alone; questioning youth can face higher distress, so it routes care to a trusted adult/counsellor, Tele-MANAS 14416, KIRAN 1800-599-0019 and Childline 1098, and addresses identity-based bullying (UNESCO safe-learning; MoHFW)
